title: Write native pi extension for br/jj workflow
description:
Replace the third-party pi-beads-extension (which was rejected during the 2026-07-31 pi package audit because it shells out to `bd` rather than `br` and its prompt templates diverge from the global-agents.md rule that pins `br` as the sole issue-tracking CLI) with a first-party extension authored in this repo.

## Motivation

The pi coding agent has no built-in awareness of the br/jj/beads pipeline codified in /etc/nixos/home-manager/server/llms/global-agents.md. Every session currently reconstructs the workflow from the AGENTS.md prose alone, which:

- Wastes context on the same procedural boilerplate each turn.
- Leaves the "empty `@` on top" invariant and the "single-writer .beads/" workspace-isolation protocol as prose the model may or may not honour.
- Provides no slash-command shortcuts for the recurring verbs (`br ready`, `br update … --status in_progress`, `jj new`, `jj squash --use-destination-message`, `jj describe -r @- -m …`).
- Offers no structural guard against the two known foot-guns already documented in global-agents.md: `jj squash` hanging on the interactive editor when both commits have descriptions, and `br` reimport silently reverting mutations.

pi-beads-extension (npm) came close in shape — small, uses pi.exec, ships 14 prompt templates keyed to beads verbs — but it hardcodes the `bd` binary name throughout both the extension source (single `pi.exec("bd", args, …)` call site at src/index.ts:58) and every prompt template ("Use the `bd` CLI to …"). We insist on `br`. A fork would need parallel patches per upstream release; a first-party extension in /etc/nixos lets the workflow drift only when we drift it.

## Reference material already in the repo

- /etc/nixos/home-manager/server/llms/global-agents.md — the canonical workflow prose. Sections to encode: "Version Control (jj — NEVER use git)", "Issue Tracking (beads/br)", "The br/jj Workflow", "Workspace isolation", "br/jj Churn", "br/jj Pair", "Plan Mode".
- /etc/nixos/home-manager/server/llms/pi/extensions/summarize.ts — the one existing hand-written pi extension in this repo; use it as the shape reference for imports, registerCommand signatures, and the ExtensionAPI/ExtensionCommandContext surface.
- /nix/store/…-pi-coding-agent-0.83.0/lib/pi/packages/coding-agent/docs/extensions.md — pi's own extension author guide. Read it first.
- /tmp/pi-review/pi-beads-extension/package/src/index.ts — the reference implementation of the shape we want (pi.exec + slash-command + state cache + prompt templates + compact-hook injection). Study, do NOT copy — it wraps the wrong binary.

## Scope

Ship a single-file TypeScript extension at home-manager/server/llms/pi/extensions/brjj.ts, plus prompt templates under home-manager/server/llms/pi/prompts/. It must:

1. Register slash commands for the high-frequency verbs. At minimum: `/br-ready`, `/br-create`, `/br-show`, `/br-update`, `/br-close`, `/br-list`, `/br-blocked`, `/br-dep`, `/br-search`, `/br-stats`, `/br-workflow`, `/jj-status`, `/jj-log`, `/jj-new`, `/jj-squash-msg` (invokes `jj squash --use-destination-message` then `jj describe -r @- -m <arg>` in one shot, per the global-agents.md guidance for avoiding the interactive-editor hang).
2. Wire pi's `compact` hook to inject the current `br ready --json` head plus the top of `jj log` into the compaction summary, so post-compact sessions resume with live workflow state rather than stale prose.
3. Wire pi's `session_start` hook to verify `jj config list --user` returns a name and email; emit a UI warning if not (mirrors the "Session prerequisite" check in global-agents.md).
4. Shell out ONLY via pi.exec (never raw child_process) — mirrors pi-beads-extension's discipline and stays inside pi's sandbox model.
5. Cache `br list`/`jj status` results with a short TTL (≤10 s) so repeated slash-command use inside one turn doesn't re-shell the same command five times.
6. Guard `br close` behind an explicit user confirmation prompt in the pair loop (the churn loop can close directly). Rationale: global-agents.md distinguishes pair from churn precisely on this axis.
7. Ship prompt templates that always reference `br` (not `bd`) and always end with the "empty `@` on top" reminder, matching global-agents.md conventions.

## Explicit non-goals

- Do NOT implement workspace-isolation orchestration (jj workspace add/forget). That's a human-driven ceremony; the extension should just print a reminder when `br/jj pair`/`br/jj churn` is invoked in a non-workspace checkout.
- Do NOT ship a task-list overlay (rpiv-todo territory). The task list IS `br list`.
- Do NOT auto-install `br` or `jj`. Both come from nixpkgs / the local flake, and the extension should hard-fail with a clear message if either is missing from PATH.

## Wiring into the module

Once the extension file lands under home-manager/server/llms/pi/extensions/brjj.ts, home.file already symlinks the whole extensions/ dir into ~/.pi/agent/extensions (see pi-config.nix), so it loads automatically on the next `just deploy`. No additional module edits needed for the extension itself; the prompt templates need matching entries under home-manager/server/llms/pi/prompts/.

## Acceptance

- `/br-ready` inside pi returns the same JSON body as `br ready --json` run in the shell, formatted for TUI display.
- `/jj-squash-msg "Introduces X"` produces one named commit and leaves `@` empty and unnamed, without opening an editor.
- The compact hook adds ≤300 tokens of workflow state to the compaction summary.
- Removing the ponytail package or toggling pellucid does not affect this extension.
- Running the pi test suite (if any lands in pi-config.nix scope) passes; at minimum, `pi -e ./home-manager/server/llms/pi/extensions/brjj.ts` loads cleanly.

title: Write native pi extension for context preservation across compaction
description:
Replace the third-party context-mode plugin (rejected during the 2026-07-31 pi package audit) with a first-party pi extension authored in /etc/nixos that captures the same value proposition — session state that survives compaction, a searchable per-project knowledge cache, and a nudge away from context-flooding shell habits — without the specific defects that killed the upstream.

## Motivation

context-mode's advertised win is real: on long research → design → implement sessions the model burns huge fractions of its context window re-reading files it already saw, re-running commands whose output it already digested, and re-fetching URLs it already summarised. A local session-scoped store keyed by tool call, plus an FTS index over past outputs, plus a compaction hook that replays the salient state, genuinely does buy back window.

The upstream implementation lost trust on this box for six independent reasons, each of which the replacement MUST address explicitly:

1. **Runtime npm install of a native addon.** context-mode's hooks/ensure-deps.mjs calls `execSync("npm install better-sqlite3 --no-save --silent")` on first hook fire. On NixOS this fails without ambient npm, and even when it succeeds the resulting `.node` is an unpinned network-fetched native binary whose glibc linkage is not guaranteed to match the pi runtime.
2. **Bundled/minified code.** ~1.5 MB across `server.bundle.mjs`, `cli.bundle.mjs`, `session-*.bundle.mjs`, `security.bundle.mjs`. Not practically auditable.
3. **Elastic-2.0 license.** Not OSI-approved; incompatible with the rest of this repo's MIT/permissive posture.
4. **systemPrompt mutation collision with ponytail.** context-mode carefully routes its context injection through pi's `context` hook because mutating `systemPrompt` invalidates prefix prompt caching on Anthropic/DeepSeek/OpenAI (their own comment cites issue #598). Ponytail, loaded alongside, mutates systemPrompt anyway, defeating that discipline. Any first-party replacement must also route through the `context` hook AND ship without any hook that mutates systemPrompt — and must document the constraint so future edits do not regress it.
5. **Aggressive bash HTTP block.** context-mode's `tool_call` hook blocks `curl`/`wget`/`fetch`/`requests.get`/`Invoke-WebRequest` unless the invocation is silent + file-output + no verbose. This breaks common recipes like `curl -sL URL | jq`, `gh api … | jq`, `curl … | tar xz`. The intent (do not flood context with raw response bodies) is defensible, the policy is too coarse.
6. **Scope creep.** ~283 files, hooks for 8 non-pi agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Kimi, Kiro, Antigravity, Codex, Gemini CLI, JetBrains Copilot, OpenClaw). Enormous surface for a "pi extension".

## Reference material already in the repo / on disk

- /tmp/pi-review/context-mode/ — the extracted upstream tarball; study `build/adapters/pi/extension.js` (861 lines, the entrypoint) for the shape of what to imitate and `hooks/ensure-deps.mjs` / `scripts/postinstall.mjs` for what NOT to do.
- /etc/nixos/home-manager/server/llms/pi/extensions/summarize.ts — the one existing hand-written pi extension in this repo; the shape reference for ExtensionAPI imports and command/hook registration.
- /nix/store/…-pi-coding-agent-0.83.0/lib/pi/packages/coding-agent/docs/extensions.md — pi's own extension author guide.
- /nix/store/…-pi-coding-agent-0.83.0/lib/pi/packages/coding-agent/docs/compaction.md — pi's compaction lifecycle; the hook contract.
- /nix/store/…-pi-coding-agent-0.83.0/lib/pi/packages/coding-agent/docs/session-format.md — session log format the extension will read to reconstruct state.
- home-manager/server/llms/global-agents.md — the workflow prose whose spirit the extension must respect (no imperative software install, jj-not-git, br-not-bd).

Read the pi docs first. The context-mode source is a shape reference, not a template — study it, do not port it.

## Scope

Ship a single-file TypeScript extension at home-manager/server/llms/pi/extensions/ctx.ts. It must:

1. **Persist session state under `~/.pi/ctx/<project-hash>.db`.** Use the sqlite runtime provided by pi (or Node ≥22.5's built-in `node:sqlite`, or Bun's `bun:sqlite`) — NEVER `execSync npm install better-sqlite3`. If the runtime has no sqlite, the extension must degrade gracefully to an in-memory Map with a UI notice, not fetch a native addon from the network. The project hash is derived the same way pi hashes session dirs (SHA256 of the workspace root, first 16 hex chars).
2. **Capture, per tool call, a compact event record** — tool name, hashed input, hashed output, timestamp, priority (a small integer 0–5 the extension assigns based on the tool: file reads/writes = 3, bash = 2, todo = 1, informational = 0). Hashes let the compaction hook detect "we already saw this exact output".
3. **On pi's `compact` / `session_before_compact` hook, inject a summary block via the `context` hook — NEVER by mutating `systemPrompt`.** The block lists: last 20 tool-call summaries above priority 2, an FTS-derived list of the top-5 files touched, and any outstanding `br ready` head (if br is installed and .beads/ exists). Bounded at ≤500 tokens.
4. **Register FOUR commands, no more**: `/ctx-stats` (per-session counts + DB path), `/ctx-search <query>` (FTS5 over past tool outputs for this project; results printed inline), `/ctx-purge` (nuke this project's DB after a confirm prompt), `/ctx-doctor` (print sqlite backend in use, DB size, event count, whether the runtime has native sqlite or degraded to Map).
5. **Do NOT register any bash-blocking `tool_call` hook.** If a coarse anti-flood policy is desired later, it belongs in a separate extension gated behind an explicit toggle in pi-config.nix, not welded to the storage layer. The description's mention of "raw response bodies flood context" is real but the correct fix is a nudge in the model's tool description (via pi's tool guidelines), not a hard block.
6. **Do NOT register any tools whose names overlap `pi-web-access`** (web_search, fetch_content, get_search_content, source_check). This extension is a context-store, not a fetcher.
7. **License MIT.** Author line: `lox`.

## Explicit non-goals

- Do NOT ship hooks for any agent other than pi. This is a pi extension in /etc/nixos, not a cross-agent product.
- Do NOT ship a bundled/minified build artifact. The extension MUST be readable TypeScript in the repo.
- Do NOT bundle better-sqlite3 or any native npm dep. Runtime sqlite only.
- Do NOT inject anything into `systemPrompt`. Use the `context` hook exclusively.
- Do NOT try to intercept or replay session state cross-project. Per-project DB, no more.
- Do NOT enable an MCP bridge or spawn any child process at load time. If a future extension wants MCP, that is a separate concern.

## Wiring

home.file already symlinks home-manager/server/llms/pi/extensions/ into ~/.pi/agent/extensions (see pi-config.nix), so the new .ts drops in on the next `just deploy`. No module edits required for the extension itself. If a runtime-detected feature (e.g. sqlite backend selection) needs a config knob, add it as an option under `piSettings` in pi-config.nix so the machine's declarative posture stays the source of truth.

## Acceptance

- Fresh session on this NixOS box loads the extension without printing any npm/native-addon warning.
- `/ctx-doctor` reports the sqlite backend it selected and a non-zero event count after a few tool calls.
- After a compaction, the post-compact system message contains the injected `<ctx-recap>` block (or equivalent tag) and no changes to the model's `systemPrompt` field.
- `/ctx-search <string>` returns hits from a prior turn's tool output within the same project.
- Uninstalling pi-web-access does not break /ctx-search; installing a second web-fetch extension does not conflict.
- Total .ts source ≤800 lines, readable, no dependencies beyond what pi's runtime already supplies.
